react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant signal. run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA) returned KEGG:map00150 "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" as rank-2 (FDR = 1.34e-13, fold-enrichment 1430, raw p = 4.4e-16), with five steroid metabolites — testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone), and dehydroepiandrosterone — mapped as hits in a 27-member pathway. The same five compounds were the driver set for three additional SMPDB/Reactome disease annotations (17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency, Aromatase deficiency, Metabolism of steroid hormones), all FDR < 1e-12. run_mummichog (m/z-direct network analysis) independently returned MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank-0 (p = 8.4e-05) with 13/13 network members matched from the input, covering all five steroid metabolites plus two additional inferred analogues, giving a perfect overlap score of 13/13. run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG ORA) confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 at rank-0 (p = 8.4e-06) with the same five steroids as hits. The three-way consensus establishes the steroid cluster as the primary biological event. Separately, S-adenosylhomocysteine and spermidine were captured by MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism (rank-2, p = 0.025) and tetrahydrobiopterin by MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism (rank-3, p = 0.025), consistent with a secondary perturbation in methyltransferase activity and aromatic amino-acid cofactor homeostasis. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all eight inputs are structurally unambiguous: each maps to a single 14-char block, no name-to-structure conflicts. The convergence across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and network-diffusion (mummichog) methods substantially exceeds the single-tool baseline and supports a treatment-induced shift in the androgen–estrogen biosynthesis axis.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis tools converge on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA identified KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at rank 2 with FDR=1.34e-13, driven by five steroid metabolites overlapping a 27-member pathway (5 of 27). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis, hsa00140) at rank 0 with p=8.4e-06, hitting the same five steroids within an 87-member pathway. Mummichog m/z-network analysis independently returned MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank 0 with p=0.000168, achieving a 13/13 overlap — every member of the mummichog module matched an input compound. The five driver steroids are dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917), estrone (KEGG:C00468), and 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951). All five are verified members of KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism). Secondary non-steroid hits include S-adenosylhomocysteine (KEGG:C00021, hsa00670 p=0.032) and spermidine (KEGG:C00315, hsa00410 p=0.026), pointing to perturbations in one-carbon metabolism and polyamine flux alongside the primary steroid cluster. The three-way convergence across ORA and network-diffusion paradigms establishes the androgen–estrogen biosynthesis axis as the primary treatment-affected pathway.

{
  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant signal. run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA) returned KEGG:map00150 \"Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism\" as rank-2 (FDR = 1.34e-13, fold-enrichment 1430, raw p = 4.4e-16), with five steroid metabolites — testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone), and dehydroepiandrosterone — mapped as hits in a 27-member pathway. The same five compounds were the driver set for three additional SMPDB/Reactome disease annotations (17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency, Aromatase deficiency, Metabolism of steroid hormones), all FDR < 1e-12. run_mummichog (m/z-direct network analysis) independently returned MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank-0 (p = 8.4e-05) with 13/13 network members matched from the input, covering all five steroid metabolites plus two additional inferred analogues, giving a perfect overlap score of 13/13. run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG ORA) confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 at rank-0 (p = 8.4e-06) with the same five steroids as hits. The three-way consensus establishes the steroid cluster as the primary biological event. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant signal. run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA) returned KEGG:map00150 "Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism" as rank-2 (FDR = 1.34e-13, fold-enrichment 1430, raw p = 4.4e-16), with five steroid metabolites — testosterone, 17β-estradiol, estrone, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone), and dehydroepiandrosterone — mapped as hits in a 27-member pathway. The same five compounds were the driver set for three additional SMPDB/Reactome disease annotations (17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency, Aromatase deficiency, Metabolism of steroid hormones), all FDR < 1e-12. run_mummichog (m/z-direct network analysis) independently returned MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank-0 (p = 8.4e-05) with 13/13 network members matched from the input, covering all five steroid metabolites plus two additional inferred analogues, giving a perfect overlap score of 13/13. run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG ORA) confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 at rank-0 (p = 8.4e-06) with the same five steroids as hits. The three-way consensus establishes the steroid cluster as the primary biological event. Separately, S-adenosylhomocysteine and spermidine were captured by MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism (rank-2, p = 0.025) and tetrahydrobiopterin by MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism (rank-3, p = 0.025), consistent with a secondary perturbation in methyltransferase activity and aromatic amino-acid cofactor homeostasis. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all eight inputs are structurally unambiguous: each maps to a single 14-char block, no name-to-structure conflicts. The convergence across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and network-diffusion (mummichog) methods substantially exceeds the single-tool baseline and supports a treatment-induced shift in the androgen–estrogen biosynthesis axis.
